questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word for the group of words.

An official pardon
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. amnesty.**

 
• **Amnesty**: an official pardon for people who have been convicted of political offences. (राजनीतिक अपराधों के लिए दोषी ठहराए गए लोगों के लिए एक आधिकारिक माफी)
 
• **Amnesia**: a partial or total loss of memory. (स्मृति का आंशिक या पूर्ण नुकसान)
 
• **Redemption**: the action of saving or being saved from sin, error, or evil. (पाप मुक्ति)
 
• **Regicide**: the action of killing a king. (राज-हत्या)

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate passive form of the given sentence.

The surgeon successfully operated upon the patient.

options.text: The patient is being successfully operated upon by the surgeon.
The surgeon has been successfully operated upon by the patient.
The patient is successfully operated upon by the surgeon.
The patient was successfully operated upon by the surgeon.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 4) i.e. the patient was successfully operated upon by the surgeon.**

 
• The active voice is in the past indefinite, hence, while making the passive voice 'was' will be used.
 
• And the subject and object of the active voice will be interchanged.
 
• All these rules are followed in option 4), hence, it is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the wrongly spelt word.

questions.question:
Identify the segment which contains the grammatical error

Pleasure cannot derive from giving pain to innocent people.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. pleasure cannot derive.**

 
• 'pleasure cannot derive' is wrongly used in option 2).
 
• In this sentence 'pleasure' is used in **passive** sense and the sentence means no one can derive pleasure from giving pain to innocent people.
 
• Hence,** 'pleasure cannot be derived' **will be used here.
 
• So, the correct sentence will be: **Pleasure cannot be derived from giving pain to innocent people.**

questions.question:
Identify the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If no substitution is required, select No substitution.

I was astonished __on the ignorance in__ the villagers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. at the ignorance of.**

 
• We cannot use 'ignorance in' because ignorance is related to someone, hence, 'ignorance of' will be used.
 
• Moreover, **astonish** takes **'at'** as a preposition with it.
 
• Thus, option 4) is the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. prosperous.**

 
• The article used before the blank is **'a',** so, we cannot use **affluent and ambitious** in the blank, since the article 'a' comes only before words that begin with a consonant sound.
 
• **Populous **means an area having a large population. This, too, doesn't fit in the context of the given sentence.
 
• **Prosperous** means **successful in material terms**. This fits the best in the context of the given sentence, hence, it will be used in the blank.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate indirect form of the given sentence.

Father said to his daughter, "I will attend your convocation tomorrow."

options.text: Father told his daughter I will attend her convocation tomorrow.
Father told his daughter that he would attend her convocation the next day.
Father told his daughter that he will attend her convocation tomorrow.
Father told his daughter that he will be attending her convocation the next day.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. Father told his daughter that he would attend her convocation the next day.**

 
• While changing direct speech into indirect speech **'said to'** is changed into **'told'** and the **present tense** is changed into **'the past tense'**.
 
• Moreover, **tomorrow** is changed into **the next day.**
 
• All these rules are followed in option 2) only, hence, the correct answer is option 2).

questions.question:
Identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Lack of formal education did not prevent Lincoln to become a great leader.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. to become.**

 
• The word **'prevent'** takes **'from'** as a preposition with it.
 
• Hence, **'prevent Lincoln from becoming'** will be used in the given sentence.
 
• So, the correct sentence will be:** Lack of formal education did not prevent Lincoln from becoming a great leader.**

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. But when their short racing careers are over, greyhounds are adopted as household pets.

B. Greyhound racing is a popular spectator sport in the United States.

C. They worry that the greyhounds would need a large space to run to get sufficient exercise.

D. Unfortunately, many people hesitate to adopt a retired racing greyhound as a pet.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. BADC.**

 
• Sentence **'B'** is the only **independent sentence**, hence, it will be the first sentence.
 
• Sentence **'A' will follow the sentence 'B'** because sentence 'B' talks about Greyhound sport and sentence 'A' talks about the Greyhounds when their career is over. 
 
• This combination i.e. BA is given in only one option i.e. 4. 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

questions.question:

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. Little did she know that I was out of job once again.

B. But all the money soon vanished into the bottomless pit of household needs.

C. I returned home with my pockets full of my earnings.

D. However, my grandmother was happy that I had become responsible.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 1) i.e. CBDA**.

 
• The only **independent sentence** from the given sentences is **'C'.** Hence, options 2 and 4 cannot be the answer.
 
• Sentence 'C' talks about the **earnings** and sentence 'B' talks about the **money** that was vanished. So, the correct pair is 'CB'.
 
• This combination is only in option 1), hence, option 1) is the correct answer.
